expectations.text: Rejects post-execution-only costing: admission control requires a static worst-case cost estimate charged before execution, with the difference against actual cost refunded afterward
expectations.evidence: 'Pre-charge a static estimate, run the query, then refund the difference.'

expectations.text: Prices cost from the query's shape and fields via a published formula an integrator can compute before sending, not from response size
expectations.evidence: The cost formula table and worked example (652 estimated).

expectations.text: Exposes both requested and actual cost on every response (such as an extensions cost object) so clients can see the pre-charge and refund accounting
expectations.evidence: 'extensions.cost' with requestedQueryCost and actualQueryCost.

expectations.text: Pins the single-query maximum cost independently of plan and states it explicitly, rejecting a plan-scaled max query cost
expectations.evidence: 'One per-query cap for every plan'; 1,000 in every column.

expectations.text: Names the portability trap motivating the plan-independent cap: a query written against a bigger plan's allowance instantly fails on a smaller-plan account
expectations.evidence: 'A query written against a Premium store fails on a Standard store.'

expectations.text: Weights mutations above reads of equivalent shape (general guidance 2-5x, with a named vendor precedent at 10x), rejecting equal costing
expectations.evidence: 'Mutations carry a fixed base cost of 10.'

expectations.text: Publishes per-field weights, not just the budget, for example scalar 0, object 1, and connections sized by their first/last pagination arguments
expectations.evidence: The table gives scalar 0, object 1 and connection 2+N×node.

expectations.text: Exposes the remaining budget and the restore rate on every response so a client can model the bucket locally
expectations.evidence: 'throttleStatus': maximumAvailable, currentlyAvailable, restoreRate.

expectations.text: Expresses the budget as bucket depth plus restore rate, burst and sustained as two numbers, not one blended figure
expectations.evidence: 'Burst and sustained are two separate numbers.'

expectations.text: Recommends a debug affordance returning a per-field cost breakdown so integrators can understand why a query costs what it costs
expectations.evidence: 'a debug flag... returns a per-field cost breakdown.'

expectations.text: Recommends a budget-introspection mechanism that costs nothing to query, so a client can check its remaining budget for free
expectations.evidence: 'a zero-cost introspection field for the live budget'.

expectations.text: Keeps structural query guards (depth ceilings, required pagination arguments, persisted queries) out of scope as schema design owned by the GraphQL API design discipline, while owning the pricing and budget policy
expectations.evidence: 'Structural guards... are schema design, covered by public-graphql-api-design.'
